Find every visible UI element in the screenshot: buttons, icons, menu items, tabs, links, text input fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns, sliders, list or table items, labels, headings, text blocks and images. Report each distinct element once, with a tight box around that element only. Scan the whole screenshot systematically, top to bottom and left to right, and check every part before you finish; do not stop early. Do not invent elements.

Each element has x1, y1, x2, y2: the left, top, right and bottom edges of its tight axis-aligned bounding box, with 0 <= x1 < x2 <= 1000 and 0 <= y1 < y2 <= 1000. Coordinates are integers on a 0 to 1000 grid of the FULL IMAGE: 0 is the left (or top) edge and 1000 the right (or bottom) edge, whatever the pixel size of the image. Never give pixel coordinates. Each element also has name: at most four words of its visible text, or a short description if it has no text.

Output contract: return exactly one JSON object {"status": ..., "elements": [...]}. status is found when you have completed the inspection, empty when there is no UI element, unknown when you could not complete it (include all recovered elements). No prose, no code fence.

Example of the schema only:
{"status":"found","elements":[{"x1":12,"y1":20,"x2":61,"y2":48,"name":"File"},{"x1":400,"y1":300,"x2":520,"y2":340,"name":"Search field"}]}
